title: I think I suck at my own game...
author: Parreirao2
selftext:
So this is a side project I've been making for a long time, a Pokemon Game for Android that started as a Virtual Pet from an esp32 and now it has so much content I don't even bother to try other official Pokémon games, at this point if I like something I see, I just make it myself on my game in my own way.

For instance, I've been making this Game Mode, which is inspired by the Big Kid Nation project, just for fun, as an alternative game mode to keep me entertained during work breaks.

If anyone's interested in it, I can definitely showcase more of the app, it has traditional battles, map with every generation regions and routes, PMD game mode, ports of games from old devices like the e-reader, contests, breeding, farms, prismatics (copied from Aniimo), TCG, etc etc...

comments.author: Riolutail
comments.body:
I can see amount of time effort spent on this project and commend you greatly. Scrolled the gallery and seems like an ambitious project looking to be a pokeverse of sorts that aims to include nearly every Pokemon game style / mechanic out there on the internet.

Gonna be honest here though, as a fellow Pokemon lover and fangame dev. Unless a large majority of the different modes you offer in your game is more polished or offers more fun/depth compared to the best respective available alternatives, it is going to be a really difficult sell for people to pick up your game over the others. If that’s not your goal though and you are just making this for yourself and for the narrow audience looking for this exact concept, you can largely ignore the rest of my feedback.

I think it’s totally fine to adapt/offer many different modes and concepts in a game, especially when they are already familiar to your target audience. But there’s probably a line where adapting too much introduces feature bloat and makes it harder for users to understand/navigate your game, especially if they only come to check out one of a handful of modes (the 2D arena mode from this post, for example).

What could potentially help is reframing your project - instead of one “game with different modes” you can instead offer it as a “platform with different individual games” to choose from. And the twist could be that your characters are persistent across the games, which I think is what u have going on? Not sure since I can’t test directly. This would help address the second issue of user navigability and their ability to understand how to play the mode they came for.

If you want to address the first issue, I think you would benefit greatly from just sitting down and focusing on one to three of the modes/games where you think you have the most unique ideas and perspectives, and honing them in a way that offers an experience that feels fun and rewarding to play, but in a DIFFERENT way compared to others in the genre. Otherwise, using this 2D Arena mode as an example, the moment big kid nation releases the version he’s been grinding and focusing on (while u had to split ur attention across all your modes), people are likely going to drop the version you worked hard on to push out for the more polished version. I couldn’t tell you how to add that differentiation, nor can i promise that your ideas won’t just get adopted by big kid nation or others that do end up seeing your games. My only recommendation is to ship features that are as unique as possible, and that are the hardest to reverse engineer (putting all your code on github publically would this part difficult). People can see/pick apart everything you give/send them on the client - the only code they cant directly see easily is non-public code running on a server.

Sorry for the long comment but hopefully something here is helpful. Best of luck you got potential

replies.author: Parreirao2
replies.body:
Woah this is the best feedback I've ever received on Reddit, or anywhere else. Thank you so much! 

I totally agree with you, the app is filled with stuff, but I promise you that everything Integrates with each other. The main concept is for the player to raise their pokemon not only by leveling but by taking care of it, that's the core of the app, that's why there's a lot of emphasis on that part (it's the main tab). As a kid, I always loved tamagotchis and digimon vipers, so I tried to bring that to Pokemon adwell.
From there I added a lot more stuff because I was the only one playing it (well, me and my gf) and I didn't want to get bored fast as this is a passion project and I tend to abandon projects once I get bored, so I started by adding wild battles (which is an adjusted replica of pokemon main games battles) then I added all the maps from all games and their respective routes and spawn pools, and that became the only way to catch legendaries (you have to unlock a region at a time), this also serves as a way to catch pokemon of your choosing and shiny hunting
Then I added minigames for those times where I just want a quick distraction and decided to make my own games and also import some from old pokemon (maybe obscure and forgotten) games to hopefully differentiate the app from others a likes, and from there everytime I felt bored and that the app was missing more things to excite me I started adding mechanics that I liked like breeding, mystery dungeon format dungeons for special items, farms to grow berries (to feed the pokemon), and some auto-battle/idle mechanics from games that I liked like afk arena, etc etc... and recently I got excited by the Big Kid Nation showcase and decided to make that as well.
I like to tinker a lot, I have made dozens of apps for my daily needs, so this project is more a "fit all in one" source for my pokemon addiction.
Everything I make for this app, I try to connect it to the main game mechanic (virtual pet), and always with the goal to make it matter in the long term.
Of course I agree with you that maybe for new players it can feel overwhelming, because they didn't go through all the stages of the app, so just getting everything at once may be a bit too much, but I hope that once I make it public (no source code, just the apk, I wasted too many hours to just give everything away), someone who feels or thinks like me, might appreciate all that is available in the app.

replies.author: Riolutail
replies.body: you are very welcome - sounds like you already have your hook and didn't even need me. definitely lead with the partner raising mechanic and be loud with it. All these other modes/features can be secondary and will fall naturally underneath as people come to your game via the primary hook and explore the features themselves if they want to
